newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks in late downturn, track long bond.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks in late downturn, track long bond.

text.p: Mexican stocks Tuesday reversed earlier gains after a late surge in U.S. Treasury bond yields, dealers and analysts said, but managed to end marginally above the pyschological 5,000-point barrier.

"We were saved by the bell. Rising long bond (30-year U.S. Treasury) yields (interst rates) make dealers nervous, and it's all down to U.S. data," a floor trader said, referring to U.S. retail sales data due Wednesday, and inflation figures due Thursday.
The leading IPC share index ended down 40.77 points, or 0.81 percent, at 5,002.88. The 30-year Treasury bond was down 15/32 to yield 6.68 percent in late dealing.
Trading volume was thin at 80.4 million shares due to market caution, dealers said.
"The bourse moved on keynote U.S. economic data. There is some nervousness and a lot of caution," said Carlos Escalante, an independent market consultant.
"The market is cautious and very selective. They take profits as soon as prices rise, then they stand aside while it falls to buy low," he added.
The IPC index had risen as high as 5,086.14 points in earlier trade before profit-taking set in, dealers said, which accelerated when the Dow Jones industrial average took a sharp dive.
The Dow ended down 101.27 points at 7,960.84.

Traders said Telefonos de Mexico weighed most on the market, ending down 30 centavos (4 cents) at 20.25 pesos ($2.60) after reaching a high of 20.95 ($2.69). The telecommunications company's American Depositary Receipts ended down $1.03125 at $52 in New York.

Dealers noted that media company Televisa, up 3.10 pesos (40 cents) to 134.10 ($17.22), was one of the few blue chips to resist the late downward trend and post sharp gains. Analysts said the stock benefited from heavy demand for a forthcoming initial public offer by television company TV Azteca.
On the broad market, sliders outpaced gainers by 48 to 45, out of a total of 121 stocks that traded.
